articles.title: Pennsylvania man accused of plotting ISIS attack arrested with rifle and 190 rounds of ammunition: DOJ
articles.summary: Jonathan Hunter Kramer allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and acquired a semiautomatic rifle before FBI agents tracked him to a Pennsylvania hotel.
articles.body: A 21-year-old Pennsylvania man accused of plotting a violent attack on behalf of ISIS was arrested after FBI agents tracked him to a hotel and seized a semiautomatic rifle, five magazines and 190 rounds of ammunition, federal prosecutors announced Tuesday. Jonathan Hunter Kramer, of Valencia, had allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS, offered to distribute explosives manuals online and said he was preparing for his "mission" but still needed a weapon before agents moved in, according to a federal criminal complaint. Kramer is charged with receiving a firearm and ammunition, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony or federal crime of terrorism, including providing or attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization. WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS The FBI had been aware since a 2023 investigation of Kramer, at the time a minor, when he was charged and adjudicated delinquent in Pennsylvania for his role in a plot to carry out a mass-casualty attack and for possessing child sexual abuse material, according to the Justice Department. Authorities began investigating him again after an anonymous tip came in on March 19, shortly after his release from a juvenile detention facility. The tipster said Kramer was ordering "mysterious" packages and "talking to his friends from before" his juvenile adjudication. Investigators said Kramer was using the online name "Hamza Al Rashid," claiming an affiliation with ISIS and offering to share explosives manuals. He allegedly wrote about preparing for his "mission" and said he was missing a "weapon." On Friday, FBI agents watched Kramer leave his home with a bag and take a rideshare to a store, where he bought a disposable phone, according to the complaint. He then met another person in the parking lot, took a long black bag from the trunk of a vehicle and traveled to a hotel in Cranberry Township, where he paid cash for a room. Witnesses at the store and hotel said the bag made a metallic clicking sound when Kramer put it down. After checking in, Kramer went to a sporting goods store, where agents saw him at the gun counter. FBI ARRESTS WOMAN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED ISIS-LINKED ATTACK ON NEW YORK STATE CAPITOL BUILDING Agents approached him when he returned to the hotel carrying two bags from the store. Searches of Kramer, his hotel room and his home turned up a semiautomatic rifle, five rifle magazines — two loaded and three capable of holding 30 rounds each — and 190 rounds of rifle ammunition, according to the complaint. Agents also found a rifle scope and bipod, an entrenchment tool, pepper spray and about 30 knives. A handwritten note read, "DoNt look For me[.] IDK what I did buT I cant live In constant Fear[.]" Attorney General Todd Blanche said the arrest came as Americans marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. "Their outstanding work thwarted this alleged attack before innocent lives could be lost," Blanche said. FBI Director Kash Patel said Kramer had been "plotting a violent attack in support of ISIS," citing his online activity and acquisition of weapons. The Justice Department did not identify a specific target for the alleged attack. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kramer was booked into the Butler County Jail and made his first court appearance Monday. Prosecutors have asked that he be held without bond, arguing that he poses a danger to the community.

articles.title: Matthew Rhys: Five things you may not know about Emmy history-maker
articles.summary: The Welsh actor became the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night at the Emmy Awards.
articles.body:
Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys has made history at the Emmys by becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night.

He was named best lead actor in a limited series for the psychological thriller The Beast In Me , and best lead actor in a comedy for his role in Widow's Bay.

Here are five things you may not already know about the history-making 51-year-old .

At the start of his career, Rhys was so desperate for work he considered joining the British Army.

In 2000, he starred alongside American actress Kathleen Turner in the West End production of The Graduate.

But for nearly two years afterwards he couldn't find work.

So he met an army officer who he said was "incredibly suspicious" of him because he was an actor, and told him "we'll be in touch".

Rhys said: "Then about a week later, I got a rejection letter from the British Army saying, 'thank you for your interest, good luck in your career'.

"And I went, 'oh my God, I can't even join the army'."

In 2006, Rhys moved to Hollywood and surrounded himself with fellow Welsh actors - including Michael Sheen and Ioan Gruffudd.

He lived with Newport-born Sheen and schoolfriend Gruffudd. He and Gruffudd both attended Welsh medium school Ysgol Glantaf in Cardiff.

In an interview in The Big Issue Cymru in 2003 , Rhys said the pair did not see each other often, despite living under the same roof, as they were both busy working.

He affectionately called their group the "LA Tafia".

In 2012, Rhys told The Independent newspaper how the trio would speak Welsh to one another, dream of good fish and chips and watch rugby together in a British pub.

Rhys met Keri Russell in Los Angeles at a kickball game in 2002, where he asked for her phone number.

During an interview on Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen, Rhys explained that he had left a drunken message on Russell's answer machine following the meeting, which he did not remember doing.

Rhys said Russell did not find the message charming "in the slightest" so did not return his call.

A decade later, the pair finally became an item when they starred together in the TV series The Americans in 2013.

They played a married couple who were Russian spies from 2013-2018.

Rhys and Russell were a couple from 2014 and had their son, Sam, in 2016. Rhys has previously told the BBC he speaks Welsh to Sam in the hope he will understand the language for life.

He joked he planned to "force" Sam to embrace Welsh culture.

Rhys is also stepdad to Russell's children River and Willa.

4. His boat is named after a famous Welsh dish

Rhys owns a 1939 wooden cruiser boat, which shares its name with a famous Welsh dish.

The boat is named Rarebit, which is also the name of a traditional Welsh meal consisting of seasoned melted cheese sauce served over hot toast.

He told the US TV show Today he didn't realise "the disaster of buying an old wooden boat" before making the purchase.

Rhys said the boat is "part of Brooklyn history" and is the same class of boat that acclaimed author Ernest Hemingway previously owned.

Rhys admitted he has tried to sell Rarebit but now hopes to work with naval architecture at Brooklyn Boatworks to turn her into something "for Brooklyn and New York" in the future.

Rhys' first language is Welsh and regularly speaks it at home in New York.

The passionate Welshman dedicated his second award "to the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurture as anyone else".

"We are a small but mighty nation. This is incredible," he said, adding, "diolch yn fawr iawn" which means "thank you very much" in Welsh.

Rhys has also been revealed as the voice of Han Solo in a new Welsh language adaptation of Star Wars.

Star Wars will be dubbed in Welsh for the first time ahead of the sci-fi classic's 50th anniversary in 2027.

Rhys told New York Times podcast The Interview that the Welsh language project brought up some unexpected feelings.

"What was weird is obviously, they'd had to translate all these things that we'd grown up with, knowing Star Wars," Rhys said.

"I was saying in Welsh things like, 'pelydr cyrchu' - it's kind of like, 'tractor beam'."

He's keen to remain connected to all things Welsh, and in 2025, Rhys took on the role of Welsh icon Richard Burton in the one-man show , Playing Burton, raising funds for the Welsh National Theatre.

Rhys said he first saw the play as a student in London more than 30 years ago and dreamed of portraying Burton ever since.

articles.title: ‘Don't turn outer space into warzone’: China slams US deployment of weapons in space
articles.summary: International News: China on Tuesday criticised the United States over its deployment of weapons in space, urging Washington to halt its military build-up in the domain a.
articles.body: China on Tuesday criticised the United States over its deployment of weapons in space, urging Washington to halt its military build-up in the domain and warning against turning outer space into a potential battlefield.The remarks came a day after US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink publicly acknowledged that the United States has “on-orbit space control weapons” capable of defending American forces against hostile action.China's foreign ministry said Beijing supports the peaceful use of outer space and opposes an arms race or the weaponisation of the domain."China stands for peaceful use of the outer space and keeping it safe, and opposes any arms race in outer space or any attempt to weaponize it and turn it into a warzone. We urge the US to stop its military build-up in the outer space, and uphold global strategic stability with concrete actions."US confirms orbital weapons, keeps details secretMeink made the disclosure while speaking at the Air & Space Forces Association’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference in Maryland on Monday. He did not identify the weapon, disclose when it was deployed or provide details about its capabilities.Also read: Satellites, missiles or something else? US admits it has 'on-orbit' weapons for first time“This is why the United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force against hostile adversary action,” Meink said.He later declined to provide further details, saying that revealing the capability could undermine its deterrent value.Meink also refused to say whether the weapon had been tested, what type of system it was or what targets it could engage.The US Space Force subsequently said “space control” encompasses missions aimed at contesting and controlling the space domain through both kinetic and non-kinetic means. Such capabilities can disrupt, degrade or, if necessary, destroy an adversary's space systems.The disclosure has triggered speculation about the nature of the weapon. Some analysts have suggested it could involve space-based electronic warfare or jamming capabilities, while others have questioned whether the announcement provides enough information to establish a credible deterrent.US expands military capabilities in spaceThe US disclosure comes as the Trump administration expands Washington's military capabilities in space and develops its proposed “Golden Dome” missile defence system.Meink said the US also has “flight-ready hardware” for space-based interceptors, which are intended to destroy incoming missiles while they are still in space.The growing focus on space warfare reflects the increasing dependence of modern militaries on satellites for communications, navigation, surveillance and targeting.China and Russia have also developed counterspace capabilities aimed at disrupting or disabling adversary satellites, raising concerns about an emerging arms race in orbit.Under the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, countries are prohibited from placing weapons of mass destruction in orbit. However, the treaty does not impose a blanket ban on conventional weapons or systems designed to interfere with or attack satellites.The US Space Force has said its operations would comply with international law, including the Outer Space Treaty and the law of armed conflict.Meink framed the development as necessary to maintain US military capabilities in an increasingly contested space domain.“It is critically important that we maintain our dominance not only in the air, but in space,” he said.

articles.title: Matthew McConaughey on why he didn’t let his son Levi have social media until 15: “He wanted it when he was 12…”
articles.summary: Matthew McConaughey’s son Levi wanted social media when he was 12. His father, actor Matthew McConaughey, still wasn’t ready to let him join. The fami.
articles.body: Matthew McConaughey’s son Levi wanted social media when he was 12. His father, actor Matthew McConaughey, still wasn’t ready to let him join. The family eventually agreed when Levi turned 15. During an appearance on the Today Show in 2023, the actor explained why he waited, what he tells his children about sharing their lives online and why he wants his 10-year-old daughter to spend more time reading and writing songs than scrolling. His comments offer a look at how one parent is approaching the question of when children should begin using social media.Why Levi had to wait until 15McConaughey said Levi had wanted social media for several years before his parents agreed. “Oh, he wanted it early on, probably when he was 12, definitely 13, definitely 14, and we waited until he was 15,” he said. The family considered the advantages and disadvantages before making the decision. “We tried to look at the upfalls and the downfalls,” McConaughey said. “We said, look, this is, it’s not like sending your kid off to college, but it is sending your kid out with a bunch of strangers into the world,” he said.“Go live your life, Levi”McConaughey’s advice to his son was worth noting. “The main thing was this, go live your life, Levi, and if you’re doing something you think is worth sharing, then share,” he said. He did not want his son to start each day thinking about what he could do for social media. “Don’t wake up every morning going like, what can I do that would be a good share? It’s not living,” the actor said. He also explained that the family has conversations about these choices because they are following the lead of the people they are raising. “It’s like we always talk about this because we’re actually following your lead,” he said.Why he wants his daughter to build her identity firstMcConaughey also spoke about his then 10-year-old daughter and his decision to delay giving her a phone. “I have a 10-year-old. She won’t be getting even a phone for a long time. She knows that, but also I want her to live in this world,” he said. He then explained what he meant by wanting children to live in the world before spending too much time online. “Get the identity live first,” McConaughey said. The actor was referring to the stage when children are still forming their identity and figuring out who they are. “We’re talking about with the book and stuff, this is when the kids, just when they’re forming the identity,” he said.“If you’re on the social media too early, the world’s telling you. A lot of strangers are telling you who you are,” he said. He questioned the effect this could have on a child’s confidence. “Should you feel confident about yourself? Should you not feel? That’s the tail wagging the dog,” he said.“I don’t want them just scrolling”The actor’s concerns are not limited to the age at which children get social media. He also spoke about how they spend their time on screens. “Also, I don’t want her just scrolling,” he said. Instead, he wants his daughter to spend time on activities that allow her to explore her interests. “I want her to writing songs or reading,” he said. He also raised the issue of attention span. “Attention span is a big thing. They get on too early,” McConaughey said. “The attention span becomes way too short if they’re on it too early,” he added.Levi is now 18 and a budding actorLevi McConaughey is now 18 and is a budding actor himself. His father’s comments about social media come as Levi moves further into adulthood and develops his own interests. McConaughey said the family waited until Levi was 15 before allowing him to join social media, despite his earlier requests. For the actor, the decision was about more than setting an age limit. He wanted his son to have time to develop his identity, experience life and decide what was worth sharing.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Colombian ex-foreign minister accused over nanny's lie detector test
articles.summary: Laura Sarabia is accused of ordering police to interrogate her nanny after cash allegedly went missing from her flat.
articles.body:
Prosecutors in Colombia have accused former foreign minister Laura Sarabia of abusing her power after she made her nanny take a lie detector test.

The scandal erupted in 2023, when Colombian news weekly Semana reported that a woman Sarabia had employed to look after her son had been hooked up to a polygraph and questioned over the alleged disappearance of a case full of cash from Sarabia's flat.

Sarabia, who was the chief of staff for President Gustavo Petro at the time, resigned in June 2023 but was later appointed as foreign minister and, following her resignation from that post, as Colombia's ambassador to the United Kingdom.

The 32-year-old was one of the closest advisers of Gustavo Petro, Colombia's first left-wing president, who governed from 2022 to August this year.

Prosecutors said Sarabia abused her position as his chief of staff by ordering police to question her nanny, Marelbys Meza, over the alleged disappearance of the cash, which was said to amount to several thousands of dollars.

Meza told Semana that she was taken by Sarabia's driver to an official building opposite the presidential palace, saying it felt like "a kidnapping".

Police officers then attached her to a polygraph machine and questioned her about the alleged disappearance of the money.

Meza denied having stolen any money during the test, and has consistently denied any wrongdoing in media interviews since.

Prosecutors allege that in ordering police to question Meza, Sarabia improperly used state resources to investigate a matter which was not related to her official post.

Sarabia rejected the accusation during a hearing, without going into further details.

She had earlier said in a social media post that her lawyers were dealing with the issue and that she respected the judicial authorities and trusted their decisions.

articles.title: Two sailors missing after tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Oman says
articles.summary: Iran says El Gaia caught fire after hitting mines, but the US says the oil tanker was struck by a missile and then a drone.
articles.body:
Two sailors are missing and 23 others have been rescued following an attack on an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, Oman says.

Oman's Maritime Security Centre said the Panama-flagged El Gaia was being towed to an Omani port on Tuesday after a fire broke out in its engine room, adding that the vessel was targeted 1.3 nautical miles (2.4km) north of the Musandam peninsula.

On Monday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the tanker hit naval mines and caught fire while passing through what they described as a restricted and unsafe route.

But the US military insisted the Iranian report was false. It said the tanker was struck by an Iranian missile last month and again by a drone over the weekend.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, meanwhile, said it had received a report of a fire breaking out on board a vessel that was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Sunday.

The Revolutionary Guards said the vessel, Sidr, caught fire after hitting a naval mine. But Saudi authorities said it was targeted by Iran and maritime security firms reported that it was hit by projectiles north of Musandam.

The International Maritime Organization says at least 22 seafarers have been killed in 79 confirmed incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the rest of the Middle East since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran at the end of February.

Also on Tuesday, Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported that "enemy drones" had targeted two fishing boats in the strait overnight near the Iranian port of Kargan, about 80km (50 miles) north-east of Musandam.

Fars, which is linked to the Revolutionary Guards, cited the deputy governor of Hormozgan province as saying that several fishermen were reported missing following the incident and that a search-and-rescue operation was under way.

Later, a spokesman for the US military's Central Command (Centcom) told the news website Axios that its forces had destroyed two boats which tried to steal a sea drone.

"Iranian small boats recently attempted to take possession of a US unmanned surface vessel, but they were unsuccessful after Centcom forcefully responded," Capt Tim Hawkins said.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, has effectively been closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran has insisted it will not give up some measure of control over the waterway and has targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

articles.title: US mortgage rates touch 7% amid Iran war, inflation; existing home sales fall 2%
articles.summary: News News: The US housing market is facing fresh pressure as mortgage rates approach 7%, adding to affordability concerns for buyers already grappling with recor.
articles.body: The US housing market is facing fresh pressure as mortgage rates approach 7%, adding to affordability concerns for buyers already grappling with record-high home prices and an uncertain economic outlook.The average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage stood at 6.76% last week, according to Freddie Mac. But daily rates have since crossed 7%, according to Mortgage News Daily, which uses a different methodology, The Wall Street Journal reported.While the 7% threshold does not by itself represent a major change in affordability, economists say it could further discourage buyers who have already been holding back from the market.“A jump in rates like this will certainly cause [prospective home buyers] to pause,” Michael Fratantoni, chief economist at the Mortgage Bankers Association, told WSJ. “They may not go ahead and put in that contract or apply for the loan.”Mortgage rates last touched 7% in January 2025, according to the Journal, but have not remained above that level for an extended period since the second half of 2023. Before 2022, 30-year mortgage rates had not reached 7% since 2001.Why are mortgage rates rising?The 30-year mortgage rate generally tracks the 10-year US Treasury yield, which briefly crossed 5% on Monday for the first time since late 2023, according to WSJ. Rates have risen amid the Iran war, persistent inflation concerns and growing US deficits, adding to a housing market already struggling with weak sales.The Federal Reserve is expected to raise its benchmark rate Wednesday for the first time in three years. The move could push mortgage rates lower if it reassures markets on inflation, or higher if investors see inflation risks worsening.The higher borrowing costs come as home sales have already been weak.The National Association of Realtors reported last week that existing-home sales fell 2% in August from the previous month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.98 million, the lowest level since June last year.The combination of high prices and borrowing costs is particularly difficult for prospective buyers because even a relatively small increase in mortgage rates can significantly raise the total interest paid over a 30-year loan.Buyers are also unlikely to be able to rely on refinancing in the near term if mortgage rates remain elevated.Earlier this year, a brief decline in rates below 6% triggered a surge of buyer interest and raised hopes of a housing-market recovery. But rates rose sharply after the US and Israel attacked Iran and have climbed further in recent weeks amid a bond-market selloff.Weak demand is increasingly prompting some sellers to reconsider putting their homes on the market.Ng said more sellers were taking a similar approach, with some choosing to wait rather than accept lower offers in a weak market.At current mortgage rates, a buyer could face a monthly mortgage payment of nearly $5,000, according to the WSJ.Inventory offers some relief There is one important difference between the current market and the housing slump of 2023: buyers now have more homes to choose from.In 2023, many homeowners with mortgages carrying rates of just 2% or 3% were reluctant to sell because moving would mean taking on a much more expensive loan. The resulting shortage of homes intensified competition among buyers and pushed prices higher.That dynamic has eased as more homeowners, tired of waiting for mortgage rates to fall, have decided to sell. Inventory is now close to pre-pandemic levels.But a return to 7% mortgage rates could weaken that improvement. Homeowners with very low existing mortgage rates may once again have little incentive to sell, potentially limiting the supply of homes available to buyers.Higher borrowing costs could also hurt new-home construction. Builders have increasingly offered mortgage-rate discounts to attract buyers in the sluggish market. As rates rise, those incentives become more expensive, potentially squeezing builders' profits and reducing their willingness to increase construction.Economists do not expect mortgage rates to return quickly to the exceptionally low levels seen during the pandemic.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: More than 100,000 people in Japan are now 100 years of age or older
articles.summary: Figures show 88% of the centenarians are women as the population continues to age and shrink.
articles.body:
The number of people aged 100 or more in Japan has exceeded 100,000 for the first time, according to the health ministry.

Figures show Japan is now home to 107,677 centenarians, the highest number in the world, of whom 88% are women. The oldest woman is Kishimoto Fuyo, a 114-year-old from Kyoto City and the oldest man is Kato Hikaru, a 112-year-old from Kumamoto.

Health Minister Kenichiro Ueno said he was "delighted that so many people are living long, healthy and active lives", citing progress in medicine and technology.

But Kenichiri also warned of the challenge the country faces in maintaining a sustainable social security system.

Experts put the long lives of the Japanese down to several factors, including a healthy diet and an active lifestyle.

The island nation's cuisine predominantly consists of fish, vegetables, and rice - and less saturated fat than many Western diets.

Older people also regularly walk, use public transport, cycle and stretch.

Japan has been aging for years and sales of adult nappies have been higher than those for babies for more than a decade.

Companies have also developed new products for the older population, including a powered exoskeleton to support moving various parts of the body and eyewear that automatically adjusts its focus.

For a population to replace itself, each woman needs to give birth to 2.1 children on average. Last year Japan's total fertility rate dropped to a record low of 1.14.

The total population is estimated to drop to 87 million by 2070, representing a 30% decline from its peak of 128 million in 2008, according to data from the National Institute of Population and Social Security research.

Residents aged 65 and older currently make up around 30% of the population and are expected to make up nearly 40% by 2070.

Japanese authorities have called the trend an "existential crisis" with Prime Minister Sanae Takichi describing the decline as a "quiet emergency".

In 2025 Japan's total population decreased in all 47 prefectures but two, and the rate of decline is accelerating.

The government's many programmes and subsidies to encourage young people to have more children do not appear to be boosting birth rates.

Experts say the reasons are complex, ranging from lower marriage rates and more women joining the workforce to the increased costs of raising children.

While immigration has risen in previous years, foreigners only make up around 3% of the population and opposition to accepting more has grown.

When Japan began its centenarian survey in 1963, there were 153 people aged 100 or over. That figure rose to 1,000 in 1981 and stood at 10,000 by 1998.

The most recent figures were released ahead of Japan's annual "Respect for the Aged" public holiday, on which the government honours those turning 100 with a personal letter and traditional sake cup.

Studies have previously cast doubt on the validity of global centenarian numbers, suggesting data errors, unreliable public records and missing birth certificates may account for elevated figures.

A government audit of family registries in Japan in 2010 uncovered more than 230,000 people listed as being aged 100 or older who were unaccounted for , some having died decades previously.

The miscounting was attributed to patchy record-keeping and suspicions that some families may have tried to hide the deaths of elderly relatives in order to claim their pensions.

Flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft squawked 7700, the transponder code used to indicate a general emergency, during the diversion.Lucknow airport activated its emergency response protocols, deploying fire and rescue teams, ambulances, medical personnel, security and terminal support.The aircraft landed safely at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport at 6.29 pm with 103 passengers and six crew members on board. It has therefore been in service with the airline for just over five years.By the time this report was filed, passengers had been deboarded and a technical team had begun inspecting the aircraft's cargo bay. A source said the initial inspection had not detected anything suggesting the presence of smoke."We haven't found anything in the cargo bay which indicates a smoke issue," the source said. Further technical inspection was underway to determine what triggered the warning.The incident comes less than two weeks after another Delhi-bound flight was diverted to Lucknow following a similar warning.On Sept 3, Air India Express flight IX 1253 from Varanasi to Delhi, carrying 155 passengers, made a precautionary landing at Lucknow after pilots received a smoke indication in the aircraft's aft cargo compartment. articles.title: Saudi Arabia: Satellite image reveals major damage that shut crucial oil pipeline
articles.summary: Experts tell BBC Verify the pipeline's closure could cut oil supplies by as much as 3.6 million barrels per day.
articles.body:
Satellite imagery shows a key oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia has been badly damaged after a strike last week, which experts have told BBC Verify could take more than a month to repair and force oil prices even higher.

The image shows the most significant damage is at a pumping station along the East-West Pipeline, which Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on to export crude oil via the Red Sea rather than through the Strait of Hormuz, where ships have been attacked by Iran and the US during their six-month war.

The Saudi government has accused Iranian-backed militias in Iraq of the pipeline strike, which followed days of renewed missile and drone attacks on south-western Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthi group - which is also backed by Iran. Saudi Arabia has retaliated by carrying out strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of western Yemen.

New satellite images also show damage to Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Air Base after a Houthi strike last week.

The Saudi government said on Tuesday it would respond "firmly" to attacks by the Houthis.

While the Houthis have been fighting a long-running civil war against Saudi-backed Yemeni pro-government forces, the group has stepped up its campaign in recent weeks.

It seized control of significant new territory across Yemen's south-western coast last week, including areas overlooking the crucial Bab al-Mandab waterway, strengthening its ability to enforce its declared blockade of Saudi shipping.

The price of a barrel of oil has surged since Saudi Arabia said on Friday it was closing the pipeline as a precaution. Brent crude was trading as high as $108 (£80) a barrel on Tuesday, down slightly from $109.80 on Monday.

Experts from trade intelligence firm Kpler said the pipeline's closure could reduce oil supplies by as much as 3.6 million barrels per day - or about 3.6% of global demand.

"Based on new information we've received, damage to the pipeline could take four to six weeks to resolve, given spare-parts availability and impaired supply chains," said Homayoun Falakshahi, Kpler's head of crude oil analysis.

Anne-Sophie Corbeau, from the Center on Global Energy Policy at Columbia University, said pipelines are "like sitting ducks" and recent strikes are a "very important signal" indicating workarounds being used to avoid the Strait of Hormuz "may not be super useful because they can be destroyed".

The Houthis have targeted other Saudi oil infrastructure with drones and missiles which has led to some operations being suspended.

There have also been attacks on military bases. New satellite images captured on Monday show damage to Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Air Base near Khamis Mushait which the Houthis said they had targeted with ballistic missiles and drones last week after it was used to carry out air strikes on Yemen.

At least three aircraft hangars or shelters appear to have been damaged at the Royal Saudi Air Force facility where US-made F-15 fighter jets are based.

The Saudi-led anti-Houthi military coalition of Arab states said on Tuesday that a Houthi missile and drone attack had injured 13 people in attacks on what the coalition said were "civilian objects".

The Houthis said Saudi Arabia had carried out with more than 50 strikes in western Yemen over the previous 24 hours.

The UN Refugee Agency has said that more than 100,000 people have been internally displaced by the renewed conflict.

Additional reporting by Barbara Metzler and Benedict Garman

articles.title: What weapon could the US have put into space?
articles.summary: The announcement by the US points to a developing field of modern warfare in the Earth's orbit.
articles.body:
The announcement by the United States that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth's orbit has raised questions about what weaponry is actually in space, and what role it could play in efforts by great powers to dominate that arena.

Washington has given away little in its announcement. Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the "on orbit" weapon was necessary to safeguard US forces against hostile enemy action, but gave no details about the weapon's capabilities or when it was put into orbit.

So what could this weapon be, and what is wider picture like for military developments in space? Who else could have similar weaponry?

Advanced militaries already deploy satellites in space for range of purposes, from supplying secure communications to reconnaissance, and providing precise location information for targeted strikes and detecting missile launches.

As warfare become more technologically advanced, analysts expect the use of military hardware in space to increase.

Dr Bleddyn Bowen, an associate fellow in military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute and associate professor in astropolitics at Durham University, said he was only able to hazard a guess about the weapon announced by the US.

"I would expect there to be some kind of electronic warfare or radio-jamming platform, possibly, this would be a non-destructive kind of anti-satellite weapon," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

Such weaponry already exists on Earth and can disrupt satellite communications, he said. "If you take out the radio links then your satellite is very useless."

Bowen also would not rule out some sort of more disruptive and riskier weaponry, which could create a lot of debris and destruction.

"Less likely would be a kinetic kill vehicle of some sort, so a vehicle that would release a projectile of some sort that could ram into a satellite and destroy it," he said.

"Possibly some sort of close inspection and grappling satellite would be another possibility as well."

But while the weapon placed in orbit appears to be a first, the US - and indeed its Russian and Chinese rivals - have had weapons that can be pointed and shot into space for some time.

In fact in the last 10 years, Russia and China have been doing a lot more manoeuvres in space, known as rendezvous and proximity operations (RPOs) - "buzzing" Western satellites.

"Theoretically, these RPO sats can become hunter-killer satellites by physically colliding with them or by nudging them out of orbit," Dr Rod Thornton, reader in Russian Defence and Security Studies at King's College, London, told the BBC.

Bowen adds that the Chinese have demonstrated "space tug capability", saying: "A vehicle can go up to a satellite, can grapple it and move it into a different orbit."

This, he says, can be a positive development - a way of removing space junk as well as knocking out working satellites.

Thornton says that what Russia lacks in space weaponry and satellites, it makes up for in missile capability.

"The Russians... have ground-based missiles which can be launched into space to strike sats in low Earth orbit. They also have ASAT missiles that can be launched from a great height by aircraft," he says.

"From the Russian point of view they see Nato as having much better and more sats than the Russian military can call up, therefore they have invested heavily in ASATs in order to 'level the battlefield' somewhat."

Thornton adds a sobering thought: "As a last resort, the Russians can also launch nuclear weapons into space and the EPM blast would 'fry' any unhardened sats over a wide expanse."

He says that, having so few satellites, Russia would be the "big winner" in any space war, which would involve "missiles fired up into space, manoeuvring sats designed to nudge/destroy them and ground-based lasers".

articles.title: Mount Etna volcanic ash stops flights at Sicily's Catania airport
articles.summary: All flights are suspended from one of Italy's busiest airports until Tuesday night.
articles.body:
All flights have been suspended from one of Italy's busiest airports because of volcanic ash released from nearby Mount Etna.

It is the second time in recent months that Catania International Airport, on the island of Sicily, has stopped flights due to emissions from Etna, which is Europe's tallest active volcano and erupts frequently.

Airport officials said arrivals and departures, which were first halted on Monday, would be suspended until 22:00 (20:00 GMT) on Tuesday.

Ongoing activity at Etna prompted the INGV Etneo Observatory to issue a red aviation alert on Monday.

In a statement on its website on Tuesday, Catania - Italy's fifth-busiest airport by passenger traffic - said further updates would follow.

It also advised passengers due to fly from Catania to check with their airline for updates before travelling to the airport.

Catania, which usually serves about 12 million passengers each year, was closed for almost a week during the peak summer season last month because of volcanic activity.

There have been calls for the airport to shut and other facilities in Sicily to be expanded because of its proximity to Etna.

The volcano, which stands at 3,324 metres (10,906ft), is about 40km (25 miles) away from the airport.

Despite air traffic disruption, August's eruption drew large crowds of onlookers to Etna's lava flows. About 1.5 million people visit Etna every year.

articles.title: Gurgaon hit-and-run: Stalking, attempt to murder charges added in FIR against Kalyan Bainsla
articles.summary: GURGAON A 33-year-old gym owner accused of deliberately ramming his speeding car into a woman biker on Gurgaon's Golf Course Road was arrested in Raja.
articles.body: GURGAON A 33-year-old gym owner accused of deliberately ramming his speeding car into a woman biker on Gurgaon's Golf Course Road was arrested in Rajasthan on Tuesday and booked for attempt to murder and stalking, police said.The police said the the accused, identified as Kalyan Bainsla also allegedly tried to flee custody after being apprehended.Kalyan Bainsla and his cousin Lovneesh, who were together when the collision took place on Sunday, were arrested from Rajgarh in Rajasthan, a short distance from Gurgaon. Police also apprehended another man, identified as Pramod, who allegedly helped Kalyan Bainsla flee from Tikri Gurjar village in Palwal.Police said Kalyan had passed indecent comments at 27-year-old biker Shivani Chauhan before allegedly hitting her with his car.Chauhan, who shared a video of the incident on Instagram, was riding an Aprilia RS 457 when she was allegedly struck from behind by Kalyan Bainsla’s Maruti Suzuki Ciaz and sent skidding on the road.After his arrest, Kalyan allegedly tried to escape from police custody on the pretext of urinating. He fell while attempting to flee and sustained injuries, following which he was given first aid at a hospital, police said.Addressing the media, Gurugram DCP (East) Sandeep Kumar said the victim had told police that Kalyan Bainsla hurled a slur at her before the incident and tried to kill her."It can be clearly seen that he deliberately hit (the biker) from the side after an argument ... the intent was to kill the victim. The victim has also told the police that the intention was to kill her," he said.Gurugram Police Commissioner Sibash Kabiraj said Kalyan Bainsla was booked under an attempt-to-murder charge after police scrutinised Instagram videos and CCTV footage.Kalyan had switched off his mobile phone and absconded after giving an interview to the media, police said. Three teams were formed to track him and he was eventually arrested in Rajasthan.According to police, on September 14, a female biker shared a video on Instagram showing that she had been struck by a car on Golf Course Road the previous morning.The Gurgaon Police tried to contact the victim, but since there was no formal complaint, it registered a suo motu case at Sector-56 police station, an officer said.Following Bainsla’s arrest, the biker, who identifies herself as ‘Siya’ on Instagram, joined the police investigation.On her complaint, police added Section 109 (attempt to murder), Section 78 (physical and digital stalking) and Section 79 (acts against modesty of a woman) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) to the FIR, the DCP said."The victim said in her complaint that the accused was stalking her and also made obscene comments. She claims that he intentionally hit her bike. We have ... arrested him from Dausa in Rajasthan. We will take him on police remand after he is produced in a city court, while the role of his friend is being verified," Kumar said.Chauhan will also be produced before the court soon for recording her statement under Section 183 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, he added. Accused's lawyer denies deliberate intentAdvocate Naveen Bainsla, counsel for the car driver, said his client fled the collision site because he feared being beaten by a mob. He also accused the biker group of speeding and provoking his client."There were around 25 to 30 bike riders at the scene. They were riding at 120 to 160 kilometres per hour. The videos shared by Siya and another rider are edited and planted," the counsel said.Kalyan Bainsla, who has claimed that he was travelling with his two cousins and a sister, said the incident was merely an accident and there was no deliberate intent.In another video released on Tuesday, Chauhan questioned why Bainsla did not stop at the scene after she was hit and thrown to the ground if the incident was an accident.She also alleged that she was targeted because she is a woman and said she could have died but was saved by the protective gear she was wearing."I feel ashamed of such people. Women feel unsafe on the roads of Delhi and Gurugram," Chauhan said.She said the two videos that have surfaced in connection with the hit-and-run case constitute sufficient evidence.Earlier, Chauhan had claimed that several men were in the car and that they appeared to be drunk."The car driver chased me. First, I did not notice the vehicle, but it passed by me at speed. The car occupants gestured to me and tried to stop me," she told reporters."The car hit me. I fell and lost consciousness. When a fellow rider tried to stop the driver and told him to stop because it was his fault, he said, 'No, no, no, it was not my fault'," she said.How Bainsla was tracedDausa Sadar SHO Yudhishthir said Bainsla was allegedly driven away from the spot by Lovneesh, while another friend, Pramod, helped him flee from Tikri Gurjar village in Palwal.Gurgaon Police has also apprehended Pramod, the SHO said.The police have impounded the car, which is registered in the name of an acquaintance of Bainsla. His cousin Lovneesh was with him in the car at the time of the incident, police said.Kalyan Bainsla, a resident of Chandhat in Palwal district, is also a realtor and claims to be an international kabaddi player. He is married and has two children.Chauhan, a Delhi resident, has completed a course in fashion designing and contested the 2022 municipal election from Kalkaji. articles.title: Nepal FM says map including Lipulekh, Kalapani 'is national commitment, not old baggage’
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Tuesday that the country’s map showing Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura — Indian territorie.
articles.body: Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Tuesday that the country’s map showing Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura — Indian territories in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh district — could never be treated as “old baggage”, clarifying remarks he made during his official visit to India in June. Khanal said the map and the constitutional amendment endorsing it represented a “shared national commitment” backed unanimously by Nepal Parliament.The clarification came after Nepali Congress lawmaker Sita Thapaliya asked whether Khanal’s statement in New Delhi that the new govt carried “no old baggage” meant it was distancing itself from decisions taken by previous govts, particularly the controversial 2020 map. “The political map of Nepal covering Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura, and the constitutional amendment endorsing it, were unanimously approved by Parliament and represent a shared national commitment of the Nepali people,” Khanal said.“They are our constitutional and sovereign documents and cannot be regarded as a burden under any circumstances,” he added, saying safeguarding Nepal’s independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, borders and national dignity remained “a fundamental and permanent responsibility of any govt”. Khanal said outstanding differences with neighbouring countries should be addressed through dialogue and cooperation.Khanal’s June 5-7 visit was his first official foreign trip after taking office. During talks with external affairs minister S Jaishankar on June 6, he said, “Nepal’s new govt carries a clear and decisive mandate for good governance, economic transformation and result-driven diplomacy. There is no old baggage, only a resolve to build a genuinely transformative relationship with our closest and most important partner, India.”Clarifying that position in Parliament, Khanal said, “The current govt wants to take relations with neighbouring and friendly countries in a transformative direction based on mutual equality, respect, trust and economic partnership, without being constrained by prejudice, narrow-mindedness or unnecessary distrust.” He added that govt and foreign ministry would pursue “clear, mature and results-oriented diplomacy” with national interest at its centre.The comments came two days before Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle’s scheduled Sept 17-18 visit to New Delhi, where he is expected to meet senior Indian ministers for talks on post-flood reconstruction, economic cooperation, energy and connectivity.The territorial dispute is particularly sensitive for India because the three areas lie near the India-Nepal-China trijunction. articles.body:
Police in Malawi are investigating the kidnapping of a British national who was abducted in the southern African nation's main city, Blantyre.

Nusrat Osman, 47, was seized at around 12:30 local time on Friday by four men who had been travelling in a grey Nissan Dualis, according to a police statement.

The authorities have offered a reward of more than $17,000 (£12,600) for "credible information" that could lead to the rescue of the mother of two young children and the prosecution of the perpetrators.

Osman was reported to have been working for a local auditing firm.

A Malawi news outlet reported that Osman's husband was in anguish about the disappearance.

"I don't know where she is or how she is. My wife is an auditor and I have no issues with anyone," he was quoted by Nyasa Times as saying.

Police said the motive behind the abduction was unknown and that so far the kidnappers have not contacted the victim's family or the authorities.

articles.title: 'We tried to smuggle contraband but got stripped' - Apocalypse
articles.summary: Two contestants from the West Midlands feature in Channel 4's survival reality series, Apocalypse .
articles.body:
A mechanic from Birmingham is one of 14 people who were left with no food or water in an abandoned American town as part of a reality series.

Apocalypse, which airs on Channel 4, sees two groups of strangers attempt to survive at a site usually used to train the military and compete for limited resources.

Louise Baker, 43, went into the challenge thinking her practical nature and DIY skills would have prepared her for the experience, but soon found out this was not the case.

"I don't just do mechanics, I do DIY, I've landscaped my garden, tiled my bathroom, I can turn my hand to pretty much anything I want to do and thought, this sounds fun. Let's give it a whirl," she told BBC Radio WM.

With nothing but the clothes on their backs, the contestants had to brave temperatures as low as -12C (10F) during the challenge and were split into two rival camps - Eastside and Westside.

As described by Channel 4, the two groups are "surrounded by the remnants of modern life", and they must "recycle, reuse and reinvent anything of use to improve their lives".

The single mother added: "For 28 days I got dropped off with seven of the strangers, and we just had to go and find our way.

"We had to find our own shelter, food, water; we had to ration. It was all different personalities as well, and these aren't all well-known influencers; most of them are just normal people.

"There is some shouting, some crying, some laughing - there's a little bit of everything, if I'm honest.

"We did try to smuggle some contraband in our trousers and our jackets, but before we went in, we got completely stripped down to make sure that we had nothing on us at all," admitted Baker.

As well as forcing the groups to learn new skills, the mechanic said the show helped her form lifelong friendships.

She said: "I've formed a really good alliance with Kiera, Kyra and Stevie. We've called ourselves The Girls.

"We've found a really good friendship bond, and I suppose we only know what we experienced in that place, so it makes our bond completely different from anything you've ever experienced."

Councillor Celia Hibbert, Wolverhampton's Reform UK group leader, also appeared on the show.

The local politician, who represents the Penn ward, said she grew up in rural Nigeria without consistent electricity or running water.

She said: "Firstly, I heard it was going to be challenging, and secondly, I heard it was going to be something extraordinary that I haven't done before. I like adventure, but I also like challenges, and I like being outside my comfort zone. This ticked all the boxes."

articles.title: China does not need to replace the US in the Gulf
articles.summary: It can gain leverage over the region without engaging in military overreach.
articles.body:
China’s diplomatic calendar this year reflects its growing international weight. A succession of prominent leaders has travelled to Beijing, including those from the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, Canada, Spain, South Korea, Pakistan and Jordan.

The recent visit by Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani to China, as well as visits by high-level officials from the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia earlier this year, confirm Beijing’s expanding role in the Gulf.

The region, which has traditionally aligned with the US, is seeing growing competition between the two powers. But this rivalry does not mean that China is seeking to replace the US. It is approaching the region through trade and technology – something that fits into the Gulf’s own economic and development interests.

The US remains the Gulf’s most important external military partner. Its defence partnerships, intelligence ties, weapons systems, naval capabilities, and military presence remain central to regional security.

For years, Washington has measured Chinese influence against its own military power. By those standards, China remains far from being able to replace the US. But that is the wrong measure of strategic success.

China has shown little interest in competing with the US on military reach in the Gulf. That is because it has benefitted directly from the security Washington has provided in the region.

For decades, the US Navy helped secure maritime routes through which Gulf energy reached Asian markets. US military power in the Gulf region contributed to the stability that allowed Chinese companies to trade, invest, build infrastructure, and purchase energy.

From the Chinese perspective, this arrangement cost little and delivered significant returns. Replacing the US security system would mean assuming the political, financial and military costs of becoming the Gulf’s security guarantor, which would not be in its interest.

Instead, China has concentrated on sectors where it can build economic leverage, seeking to become as important to Gulf states’ economies as Washington is in the region’s security architecture.

Today, Chinese state-owned firms hold stakes in key Gulf infrastructure, such as ports. For example, COSCO Shipping Ports holds a controlling stake in the joint venture operating the CSP Abu Dhabi Terminal at Khalifa Port in the UAE.

Chinese companies are also increasingly connected to sectors that will shape the region’s future, including renewable energy, telecommunications, manufacturing, logistics, electric vehicles, and digital infrastructure.

Once these systems become interconnected through financing, contracts, and trade, disengagement carries substantial economic costs. An aircraft carrier can leave, and a troop deployment can be reduced, but leverage and stakes in ports, factories, telecommunications networks, and supply chains are harder to undo.

China’s approach does not require Gulf governments to become politically pro-Beijing. It only needs an openly anti-China position to become economically too costly.

For the Gulf states, there is no contradiction in seeking strong ties with both powers. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar each want US security cooperation and advanced Western technology while also seeking Chinese markets, manufacturing capacity, investment, and access to Asian economic networks.

Their objective is to avoid excessive dependence on either power. Their strategy is pursuing diversification, hedging, and strategic autonomy in an increasingly multipolar international system.

The US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and damaged US bases across the Gulf, including Al Udeid in Qatar, demonstrated why this strategy is so crucial. Excessive dependence on a single actor or area creates vulnerability, whether that dependence involves a single security provider, export market, shipping route, technology ecosystem, or source of capital.

For the Gulf states, diversification is therefore a necessity, a form of risk management. They are positioning themselves for an international system in which US power remains important but is no longer the only source of economic, political, and technological influence.

Diversification is being pursued not just in the security sphere. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and other regional states are attempting to build economies beyond hydrocarbons. Artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, and logistics are becoming central to their national strategies.

Artificial intelligence (AI) in particular shows what is at stake. Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN and the UAE’s G42 reflect national ambitions to build AI industries. AI in turn depends on advanced chips, data centres, energy, computing infrastructure, capital, and skilled workers.

The Gulf states are seeking partners who can contribute to the capital, technology, infrastructure, and industrial partnerships required to build these more diversified economies.

Washington should therefore reconsider how it measures strategic power.

The decisive question may no longer be how many bases a country possesses in a region, but how difficult that country is to remove from the regional system.

The US remains deeply embedded in the Gulf through defence relationships, intelligence cooperation, financial institutions, universities, technology companies, and diplomatic partnerships.

China is creating a different form of integration, as trade, infrastructure, technology, and investment generate long-term interests that markets can translate into leverage.

Washington need not force Gulf governments to choose between the US and China in every sector. Legitimate security concerns remain over advanced semiconductors, artificial intelligence, telecommunications, sensitive data, and dual-use technologies. Those sectors require clear safeguards.

The US’s better option is to compete. It should offer superior technology, credible financing, and deeper industrial partnerships, playing a meaningful role in the Gulf’s economic transformation.

Security guarantees remain essential, but they no longer guarantee primacy across every sector.

articles.title: In 2021, a British Columbia woman allowed limited tree trimming; neighbours cut far more for a Shuswap Lake view, and a judge ordered them to pay $34,064 in damages
articles.summary: US News: A British Columbia woman who allowed her neighbours to trim some trees in 2021 later found that much more had been cut down to improve their view of S.
articles.body: A British Columbia woman who allowed her neighbours to trim some trees in 2021 later found that much more had been cut down to improve their view of Shuswap Lake. A provincial court judge has now ruled that the neighbours trespassed on her property and ordered them to pay $34,064 in damages.The case involved Sicamous resident Jacalyn Hays and several neighbours who wanted a better view of the lake, Info News reported. Hays had agreed to limited tree trimming, but the court found that the work went far beyond what she had permitted.Hays said her backyard had once been a “shaded oasis” but became “unbearable” after the trees were cut. She was also concerned about the stability of the slope near her property, which had experienced a mudslide in 2012.The dispute began in July 2021 when Hays’ neighbour, Alan Fenton, approached her about trimming trees on her property. She agreed, but allowed small saplings to be cut only if they were no more than three inches in diameter. Mature trees could only be cut to a height of six or seven feet.Trees cut beyond the agreed limitsHays also asked that the tree trimmings be removed because she considered them a fire hazard. According to the court decision, she specifically told Fenton not to cut the larger trees on the hillside closer to her home.Those trees were important to Hays for two reasons. They helped stabilise the slope and provided shade to her property during summer.The morning after giving permission, Hays left the area and did not return until October. When she came back to Sicamous, she found tree trimmings scattered across the ground. She also found that some trees had been cut more than she had allowed.Hays later left again and returned the following July. By then, she found further damage. Several mature trees had been cut by 20 to 40 feet, while a mature birch tree that was about 50 feet tall had been completely cut down.The cutting had changed the condition of her backyard. Hays said she had lost the shade that had previously made the yard comfortable. She was also concerned about what the removal of the larger trees could mean for the hillside.Neighbours said they followed instructionsHays took legal action against Alan Fenton, Elizabeth Fenton, Lee Fenton, Cheryl Fenton, William Olthius and Shelly Fenton. She argued that the group had entered her property and cut down trees without her permission.Alan and Elizabeth Fenton, who were in their 80s, died sometime after the events. The remaining defendants told the court that they believed they had received clear instructions from Alan about what work they were allowed to carry out.However, Hays had recorded a conversation with Alan while he was still alive. Judge George Leven considered the recording when assessing what had happened.“From that recording, I conclude that… Alan Fenton was apologetic and acknowledged at the very least, that he and the other defendants had made a serious mistake and were in the wrong,” the judge said.The decision also referred to a comment made by Bill Olthius during the events. He said, “Look, we got her approval…let’s don’t worry about it … let’s just get it done.”For Judge Leven, the comment showed that there was confusion about the extent of the permission Hays had given. The judge said the neighbours could have easily checked what they were allowed to do before cutting the trees.Judge says a call could have avoided the disputeJudge Leven said the neighbours should have confirmed exactly what Hays had agreed to before carrying out the work.“A simple telephone call or email could easily have clarified any confusion,” the Judge said. “But they proceeded without taking this simple precaution.”The judge said it would have taken almost no effort to contact Hays and confirm the instructions. Instead, the trees were cut and the neighbours benefited from the work because it improved their view of Shuswap Lake.Judge Leven ruled that all the defendants had benefited from the cutting and were liable for trespass.The court ordered them to pay Hays $34,064. The amount was intended to cover the cost of replacing the trees, an $18,000 shade structure and two air conditioning units.The judge also said Hays could have received another $5,000 to $10,000 in damages because she could no longer enjoy her yard in the way she had before the trees were removed. However, the court could not award more because the small claims court maximum of $35,000 had already been reached.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A 1.2-million-sq-ft San Francisco mall was foreclosed and a buyer walked away; a new bid would add 6 basketball courts, 8 volleyball courts and a sports high school
articles.summary: US News: San Francisco’s struggling downtown mall could get a second life as a major sports destination. The San Francisco Standard and San Francisco Chronicle.
articles.body: San Francisco’s struggling downtown mall could get a second life as a major sports destination. The San Francisco Standard and San Francisco Chronicle report that Urban Land Development and TMG Partners have submitted a bid to transform the shuttered San Francisco Centre into a multilevel complex featuring six basketball courts, eight volleyball courts, retail, dining and a sports-focused high school. The proposal follows the collapse of an earlier deal to buy the 1.2-million-square-foot property. After its former owners defaulted on their debt, the mall was foreclosed on by lenders, while prospective buyers Presidio Bay Ventures and Prado Group later withdrew from their purchase agreement. CBRE subsequently returned the property to the market and received multiple bids before the latest bidding window closed, with the bondholder owners expected to choose a buyer in the coming weeks.From empty mall to sports destinationThe ULD and TMG proposal would divide the massive property into several distinct uses. The lower levels would retain retail and food offerings accessible to the public, while upper floors would focus on sports, entertainment and education.At the centre of the plan is a basketball-focused entertainment venue. The third floor would feature numerous basketball games and hoops, along with a restaurant and sports bar. The concept is being compared to Topgolf, but built around basketball rather than golf. The venue could also host private parties and corporate events.One floor above, the developers envision six full-size hardwood basketball courts for private training camps. The programme would be connected to an organisation founded by NBA coach and Bay Area native Phil Handy, who is on the Philadelphia 76ers’ coaching staff. The next floor would contain eight volleyball courts, which could be rented for games, tournaments and other events. At the top of the building, the proposal calls for a sports-focused high school, potentially bringing students into the centre on a daily basis.Retail would still have a roleThe proposal does not completely abandon the mall’s original purpose. Two floors would remain dedicated to retail, while an underground food court would serve visitors. The lower portions of the property would be open to the public, while some of the sports and educational areas would be restricted to members, programme participants and students.The idea is to create a destination that attracts people for reasons beyond shopping, particularly office workers and residents in the surrounding Mid-Market and Union Square neighbourhoods. That could be important for a property that has struggled as traditional retail has declined. The mall closed in February after years of tenant departures and financial problems, including the exits of major anchors such as Nordstrom and Bloomingdale’s.A difficult road backThe proposed redevelopment is arriving at a particularly complicated moment for San Francisco Centre. The previous $130-million purchase proposal from Presidio Bay and Prado Group collapsed in July after months of due diligence and negotiations. Their withdrawal sent the property back to the market and left lenders searching for another path forward.The new bid also comes as ULD faces its own financial challenges. The company has defaulted on two properties this year, while buildings connected to the firm have faced foreclosure, according to The Standard. TMG Partners, meanwhile, has a substantial Bay Area footprint and owns the nearby Metreon. The firm is expected to provide much of the capital if its partnership with ULD is selected.The property also has historic elements that must be preserved, including its distinctive dome, adding another layer of complexity to any redevelopment. For now, the sports-centre concept remains just a proposal. The owners have not selected a winning bid, and there is no guarantee that the ambitious basketball-and-volleyball vision will become reality. But after years of vacancies, foreclosures and failed deals, San Francisco Centre may finally have a plan that asks shoppers to do something very different: come downtown to play.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: GPS tracking of bailed suspects to start next year, says John Swinney
articles.summary: A pilot scheme in Tayside, Central and Fife is expected to start in 2027, the first minister has announced.
articles.body:
GPS tracking of people on bail, including those suspected of domestic abuse, is to begin in parts of central Scotland next year, John Swinney has confirmed.

The first minister updated parliament on his plans for a pilot scheme in Tayside, Fife and Central during a Scottish Parliament debate on tackling violence against women.

It came after he spoke to domestic abuse survivors and relatives of victims at a Holyrood meeting hosted by Scottish Conservative leader Russell Findlay.

The government has been criticised over the slow rollout of GPS equipment, which is used far less in Scotland than in some other countries.

Swinney announced plans for the GPS tracking pilot in the annual programme for government earlier this month.

He confirmed to parliament on Tuesday that regulations to launch the pilot scheme in the Tayside, Central and Fife sheriffdoms - to be led by Sheriff Principal Gillian Anne Wade KC - would be laid before the October recess, and that ministers were aiming to begin the rollout next year.

He insisted the pilot would be "subject to robust local arrangements" to ensure public safety.

Pilot tracking domestic abuse suspects to begin in 2027 - Swinney tells Holyrood

Calls for GPS monitoring of domestic abuse suspects after murder

We saw signs of domestic abuse, but we didn't know how to protect Stacy

The programme for government also included plans to make permanent a £2m fund providing practical and financial support to women and children escaping abusive partners.

The government has further vowed multi-year funding for charities that deliver crisis support to women and girls.

And it announced plans to recognise misogyny as a "distinct form of prejudice and abuse", alongside a public health campaign to target toxic male behaviour.

However, the brother of a woman murdered by her estranged husband in Renfrewshire this year said previously that the proposals were not "anywhere near good enough".

Stacy Hunter, 35, was killed by Jim Mair, 43, at her home near Houston in July while he was on bail for attacking her. His body was found nearby.

Sean Hunter - who attended the meeting at Holyrood before the debate - has called for immediate action to prevent further deaths.

Speaking to BBC Scotland News the day after his sister would have celebrated her 36th birthday, he said GPS monitoring would "absolutely make a difference".

But he called for authorities to consider more specific offences when making decisions about bailing domestic abuse suspects.

"There's so much - strangulation, attempted murder - that's going on that's being overlooked because it's coming under this umbrella of domestic violence," Sean said. "That shouldn't be the case.

"When these people commit these crimes they need to be looked at for what they are and kept from harming more people."

Liz Shanks, whose former partner Chris Forrest was jailed in 2022 for attacking her over a three-year period , also spoke to the first minister at Holyrood.

The campaigner said survivors and victims had been let down by the justice system and that the meeting must not be a "media stunt".

She called for reforms to tackle domestic abuse, and warned that victims may be reluctant to come forward if they do not feel the justice system is dealing with the issue robustly.

Opening the debate, Swinney said the so-called "manosphere" and extreme pornography had "warped views and attitudes in disturbing and profoundly harmful ways".

He vowed the government would take a "public health preventative approach" to tackle violence against women and push for stronger regulations of social media sites.

The first minister told MSPs: "We will work to build a Scotland where everyone is safe, accepted, and respected, where women and girls live free from all forms of violence, abuse and exploitation, and where all are free of the attitudes and stereotypes that perpetuate inequality."

However, opposition MSPs noted a 14% annual increase in domestic abuse charges last year.

Scottish Labour's Jackie Baillie agreed with Swinney's "sincere" willingness to tackle violence against women, but said a "multi-faceted" approach was required, including a misogyny reduction unit, extra work in schools and investment in police.

Conservative MSP Stephen Kerr warned that GPS tracking was a "technology, not necessarily a solution", calling for more investment in community resources.

Scottish Tory leader Russell Findlay praised the "extraordinary bravery" of survivors but urged ministers to strengthen bail laws and "robustly enforce breaches".

He also called for ministers to scrap "ludicrous" sentencing guidelines that encourage rehabilitation rather than jail terms for under-25s.

Scottish Green co-leader Ross Greer said extra measures were required to ensure that education in schools about harmful attitudes was being consistently delivered, and raised concerns about low reporting rates.

He also called for men to "contest" harmful views expressed by their peers.

Liberal Democrat MSP Yi-pei Chou Turvey called for the government to immediately launch its plans for special sexual offences court. Swinney told MSPs ministers planned to provide funding for the scheme in the next financial year.

Reform UK Scotland's Amanda Lindsay questioned whether "some groups" committed more sexual crimes than others, calling for more data on offences against women and girls.

How does electronic tagging work in Scotland?

In Scotland, electronic tagging has mainly relied on older radio frequency (RF) equipment which is focused on home curfews or detention.

These devices are linked to a receiver in the offender's home and cannot track movements away from the property.

In 2016, an expert group recommended that Scottish authorities adopt GPS monitoring.

However, last year, the independent public body Community Justice Scotland (CJS) issued an urgent National Improvement Recommendation to the government urging it to accelerate the expansion of more sophisticated monitoring systems, including GPS.

The technology has been widely used in England and Wales since 2018 and there are plans to start imposing new restriction zones on offenders this autumn .

Victim Support Scotland welcomed the Scottish government's GPS tracking pilot, but warned it relied on a "swift emergency response to be effective" and would not be a "catch-all solution".

Carol Eden, the organisation's head of communications and external affairs, said that it had "deep concerns about the safeguards in relation to bail".

She added that more needed to be done to "protect women who are subject to domestic violence in particular, including strengthening risk assessments and incorporating victim feedback".

articles.title: Reform's Dan Thomas resigns as Wales leader after arrest
articles.summary: Gwent Police said he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.
articles.body:
Reform UK's Dan Thomas has quit as the party's Welsh leader, after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour on Sunday.

Gwent Police said a 45-year-old man from Aberbargoed, in Caerphilly was bailed pending further enquiries.

In a statement issued by his party, Thomas said he was "standing down" from his position due to personal reasons. He said he had been "released without charge" and had "done nothing wrong".

Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates said the news demonstrated Farage's' "appalling judgement".

Thomas did not take part in First Minister's Questions earlier today.

He was first elected to serve the seat of Casnewydd Islwyn in the Senedd elections in May, where his party went from having two politicians in Cardiff Bay to 34 .

Reform came second behind Plaid Cymru in the vote, with Thomas becoming leader of the opposition in the Senedd.

Thomas said: "It has been the honour of my life to have been the leader of Reform Wales and see this party go from zero to 34 elected members and become the largest opposition group in Welsh history.

"With deep regret, I am now standing down from this position due to personal reasons.

"Over the weekend, I was reported to the police and was released without charge."

He added: "I will continue to serve my constituents in Casnewydd Islwyn and will fully back whoever the group selects as its next leader."

The news came on the same day that Reform MS Sarah Cooper-Lesadd defected to Plaid Cymru .

Who is Reform UK's Welsh leader Dan Thomas?

Dan Thomas: The ex-London council leader in charge of big Senedd opposition group

Gwent Police said: "On Sunday 13 September a 45-year-old man, from the Aberbargoed area, was arrested on suspicion of assault and engaging in controlling/coercive behaviour.

"He has been bailed pending further enquiries."

Ken Skates, leader of Welsh Labour, told the Press Association: "This is quite incredible news and many questions will need to be answered.

"Dan Thomas was a personal pick by Nigel Farage and this will surely demonstrate the appalling judgement of the Reform UK leader."

Mims Davies, the Conservative Shadow Secretary of State for Wales said: "Reform are hitting the news for all the wrong reasons - massive crypto donations, on top of the jailing of Nathan Gill for pro-Russian bribery .

"All this raises serious and deep questions about Reform's judgement and leadership at every level."

Welsh Liberal Democrat Leader, Jane Dodds, said: "The wheels are rapidly coming off Reform in Wales and the entire country."

Thomas grew up in Blackwood in the south Wales valleys.

Both his grandfather and great grandfather were miners, he said, and he had "fond memories" of growing up in Wales - but left when he became an adult because "good opportunities" there were "few and far between".

He worked in financial services in London and became a councillor, and later Conservative leader, at Barnet council in the north of the capital.

During this time Thomas stood for the Conservatives in the Islwyn constituency at the 2010 and 2017 general elections, coming second to Labour's Chris Evans on both occasions.

Thomas then led Barnet council from 2019 to 2022, eventually becoming opposition leader after Labour won the local election there until May 2024.

In June 2025 Thomas defected from the Conservatives to Reform, and at the end of the year resigned from the council.

Local media quoted him saying he moved away from Barnet so that he and his wife could raise their young sons in the countryside and live closer to their families in south Wales.
